tagline: A UNESCO river city where the wine, the cellars and the coast all line one iconic waterway — and the Douro's tourism boats prove the water already sells.
summary: Porto is built up the steep banks of the Douro, facing Vila Nova de Gaia and its port-wine cellars across the river, with the estuary opening to the Atlantic at Foz do Douro and Matosinhos to the north. The Douro is already a heavily used tourism waterway — rabelo cruise boats, river cruises up to the Douro Valley — but offers nothing fast or on-demand for point-to-point travel between the riverfront districts, the coast and up-valley towns. A clean foiling tier adds speed and utility to a river the city already celebrates.
competitive_landscape: The Douro carries a large heritage-cruise and scenic-tour fleet (six-bridges cruises, multi-day Douro Valley boats), but no fast commuter or on-demand premium service across the urban river or out to the coast. The water is proven for leisure and entrenched in Porto's identity; the gap is utility — quick hops between Ribeira, Gaia, Foz and Matosinhos, and faster reach to the up-valley wine towns — which a foiling tier supplies without competing with the slow scenic boats.

demand_signals.label: Douro river-tourism economy
demand_signals.note: Porto's six-bridges cruises and Douro Valley river boats carry very large annual visitor volumes — a deep, proven willingness to travel by water on this river.

demand_signals.label: Gaia port-wine cellars
demand_signals.note: Vila Nova de Gaia's riverfront cellar district draws constant cross-river visitor flow on foot over crowded bridges — a short, dense water-hop opportunity.

demand_signals.label: Foz & Matosinhos coast
demand_signals.note: The affluent Foz do Douro waterfront and the Matosinhos port/beach district sit at the river mouth, slow by tram and road from the centre.

journeys.today: A slow historic tram or a congested drive down to the river mouth.
journeys.with_navier: A quick ~3 nm foiling run down the Douro to the coast, well inside the all-electric envelope.

journeys.today: A full-day scenic cruise or a slow up-valley road.
journeys.with_navier: A faster foiling connection up the regulated Douro toward the wine-valley towns — a premium time-saver on a heritage route.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The urban-river and coastal mesh — Ribeira↔Gaia (~0.3 nm), Ribeira↔Foz (~3 nm), Foz↔Matosinhos (~2 nm) and up-valley Douro hops — sits far inside the 70 nm all-electric range. The river is dam-regulated and sheltered, ideal calm-water foiling, with low wash for the UNESCO riverfront.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The Douro is pure Pioneer II territory; Quanta-LR hybrid range would open Atlantic coastal line-haul north toward Viana do Castelo or south toward Aveiro without charging build-out, extending beyond the river core.

precedents.what: Electric passenger boats upgrading a celebrated urban river's transport tier
precedents.why_it_matters: Shows clean fast boats adding daily utility to a river already iconic for tourism — directly parallel to layering foiling mobility onto the Douro.

regulatory_note: Douro navigation is managed by APDL (the Douro and Leixões port authority) and the Portuguese maritime authority, with the river dam-regulated and the Porto riverfront a UNESCO World Heritage site favouring low-wash, zero-emission craft. EU green-transport funding and Porto's heritage-protection posture both support an electric tier; existing cruise quays offer ready boarding infrastructure.
seasonality: A strong summer-to-autumn tourism peak (May–October), with the wine-harvest season lifting up-valley traffic; the urban cross-river and coastal hops run year-round in Porto's mild Atlantic climate. Winter Douro flood-flow management is the main navigational constraint up-valley.
